research_question: On a fixed LongMemEval-S development subset, under one pinned answer model, identical prompt contract, and one evaluator contract, does deterministic BM25 cross-session retrieval (EXT-B5) produce observable answer-quality improvement over no cross-session memory (EXT-B0), and at what token, latency, storage, and execution cost?
primary_metric: paired semantic correctness difference EXT-B5 minus EXT-B0

selection.algorithm: hash-ranked fixed quotas by question_type, with four abstention cases selected first without reading reference answers or model outputs

answer_model.capability_status: development candidate; must pass non-overlapping screening and must not be described as competitive or parity-capable before evidence

evaluator.semantic_status: must calibrate before formal correctness claims

stopping_rules: Stop before inference if the committed development manifest is absent or its hash differs.
Stop and retain evidence if dataset or model revision cannot be verified.
Do not stop because observed results favor either baseline.
A run with fewer than 20 paired cases is expanded smoke only.
failure_policy: Retain every timeout, crash, malformed output, dependency error, and invalid evaluator output as an immutable attempt record.
retry_policy: At most one infrastructure retry; attempt 1 is never overwritten, and analysis follows the terminal-attempt policy declared before rerun.
exclusion_policy: No post-inference exclusions. Dataset-invalid cases may only be excluded by a versioned pre-inference manifest with preserved rationale.
analysis_plan: Report paired correctness, exact confidence interval, McNemar test when applicable, question-type breakdown, retrieval diagnostics, and incremental token latency storage and monetary cost per additional correct answer.
